requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The `regexp` predefined function has the syntax regexp [@nocase] (in template (value) any inpar, in template (present) any expression, in integer groupno) return any_character_string_type.
requirements.original:
regexp [@nocase] (
    in template (value) any inpar,
    in template (present) any expression,
    in integer groupno
  ) return any_character_string_type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The `regexp` function SHALL first match the inpar actual parameter (or, if inpar is a template, its value equivalent) against the expression actual parameter according to the pattern matching rules of clause B.1.5.
requirements.original: This function first matches the parameter inpar (or in case inpar is a template, its value equivalent) against the expression in the second parameter according to the pattern matching specified in clause B.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism, the `regexp` function SHALL process it as if it was a character pattern as described in clause B.1.5.
requirements.original: If expression is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism, it shall be processed by this predefined function as if it was a character pattern as described in clause B.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, the matching of that call SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way as specified in clause B.1.5.6.
requirements.original: If the @nocase modifier is present, this and all subsequent matchings shall be done in a case-insensitive way, as specified in clause B.1.5.6.

readings: If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, the matching of that call SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way.
If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, that matching and all matchings performed subsequently (e.g. in later statements or calls) SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way.
ambiguity.issue: "this and all subsequent matchings" has no defined referent for "subsequent"; the reading limited to the matching(s) of the same call is chosen because the modifier is part of the call syntax.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is a literal without explicitly given type
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a literal whose type is not explicitly given, the type of inpar SHALL be retrieved from the value contents.
requirements.original: If inpar is a literal (i.e. type is not explicitly given) the corresponding type shall be retrieved from the value contents.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the matching of inpar against expression is unsuccessful, the `regexp` function SHALL return an empty string.
requirements.original: If this matching is unsuccessful, an empty string shall be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the matching of inpar against expression is successful, the `regexp` function SHALL return the substring of inpar that matched the group of expression with group number groupno.
requirements.original: If this matching is successful, the substring of inpar shall be returned, which matched the groupno-s group of expression during the matching.

requirements.subject: ent:group-number
requirements.canonical: The group numbers of an expression of `regexp` ARE assigned in the order of occurrence of the opening bracket of each group, counting from 0 in steps of 1.
requirements.original: Group numbers are assigned by the order of occurrences of the opening bracket of a group and counted starting from 0 by step 1.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The inpar and expression actual parameters of `regexp` SHALL each be a value or a template of `charstring` or `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: The parameters inpar and expression shall be a value or a template of charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value matching mechanism only.
requirements.original: In case inpar is a template, it shall contain the specific value matching mechanism only.

readings: If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value matching mechanism only.
If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value or character pattern matching mechanism only.
ambiguity.issue: This sentence allows only specific value, while the error cause in C.4.1-s018 only lists matching mechanisms other than specific value or character pattern; the text of this sentence (together with the formal parameter restriction template (value)) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain only the specific value or pattern matching mechanisms.
requirements.original: When expression is a template it shall contain the specific value or pattern matching mechanisms only.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The groupno actual parameter of `regexp` SHALL be a non-negative integer.
requirements.original: The parameter groupno shall be a non-negative integer.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The type of the character string returned by `regexp` IS the root type of the inpar actual parameter.
requirements.original: The type of the character string returned is the root type of inpar.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: Unlike other well-known regular expression implementations, the `regexp` function matches the whole inpar string instead of only a substring.
requirements.original: NOTE: This function differs from other well-known regular expression matching implementations in that: a) It matches the whole inpar string instead of only a substring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: Unlike some other regular expression implementations, the `regexp` function starts counting groups from 0, and group 0 IS the first group rather than the whole matched substring.
requirements.original: b) It starts counting groups from 0, while in some other implementations the first group is referenced by 1 and the whole substring matched by the expression is referenced by 0.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `regexp` in addition to the error causes specific to `regexp`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a template that contains a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: when inpar is a template, it contains other matching mechanism than specific value or character pattern;

readings: An error SHALL occur if inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern.
An error SHALL occur if inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value (as required by C.4.1-s010).
ambiguity.issue: Conflicts with C.4.1-s010, which allows only the specific value matching mechanism for inpar; the literal text of this error cause is used.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is a template that contains a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: when expression is a template, it contains other matching mechanism than specific value or character pattern;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is charstring and expression is universal charstring
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is of `charstring` type and the expression actual parameter is of `universal charstring` type, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar is of charstring type and expression is of universal charstring type;`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: If the groupno actual parameter of `regexp` is a negative integer, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: groupno is a negative integer;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression has no group with number groupno
requirements.canonical: If the expression of `regexp` contains no group with group number groupno, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: there is no groupno -s group in expression.

non_requirement.reason: example caption; example code C.4.1-s023 is linked to the regexp requirements
